correctness.rationale: Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus 17. Character-pullback maps between the sixteen quotients and the Jacobian give a kernel killed by 16 and preserve 5-divisible groups. Supersingular elliptic conditions come from the Legendre Hasse polynomial. If h>=4 a shared triple reduces to 21 finite field candidates; if h=3 and no shared triple, exactly two symbolic coprimality identities force the genus-two Hasse determinant nonzero. Both critical computations replay by exact field and polynomial arithmetic; universal bounds and witness follow.

value.rationale: The lower bound and attainment solve a natural moduli-wide minimal p-rank question in a genus-17 family; the equality h=4 locus has a unique branch orbit. A structural compatibility obstruction ties four supersingular elliptic quotients to an ordinary genus-two quotient; it is more than an arbitrary parameter substitution or a finite table. The resulting sharp a-number and Newton polygon inform Jacobian arithmetic.
